findings.detail: The plain index commit records the whole index, so the scope guarantee depends on the coordinator index only ever holding .shiki. I confirmed this holds today (only .shiki-scoped adds run with cwd=target; every git push / git add -A runs in a worktree). Already acknowledged in the task's own pre_pr findings; documented, not enforced at the commit site. Non-blocking.

findings.detail: The `git commit --no-verify` runs check=False inside the finally, so a missing user.name/user.email would swallow the failure and revert to the aborting-merge behavior. Irrelevant in production (identity always configured; tests set it). Non-blocking, matches the finding already recorded on the task.

scope:
Make the loop's coordinator-side mirror writes survive a later `git merge origin/main` without a manual step. The previous implementation staged them; measurement shows staging is not enough.

MEASURED IN A MINIMAL REPRO, with the colliding path byte-identical to the incoming version:
  staged + FAST-FORWARD merge          -> succeeds
  staged + NON-fast-forward merge      -> 'error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge'
  committed + NON-fast-forward merge   -> 'Merge made by the ort strategy', clean
The coordinator always carries its own commits, so it is ALWAYS the non-fast-forward case. `git add` only renamed the failure.

COMMIT the coordinator's `.shiki` writes, do not merely stage them. Keep every other property the previous implementation established: one covering point that every effector in `execute_action` passes through (eleven branches, `:1983`-`:2227`) so a future effector is covered by construction; scoped to `.shiki` so nothing outside the mirror is ever touched; and never staging a deletion, so the append-only mirror cannot be emptied by this path.

THE REMOVED CONSTRAINT. The previous contract's non-goal 'Committing in the coordinator — the local branch must not advance' was asserted without measurement and is exactly what made the design unable to satisfy its own criterion. It is REMOVED. The coordinator's branch is a disposable execution surface that is never merged anywhere, so advancing it costs nothing. Commit only the mirror; never commit anything outside `.shiki`.

WHAT REMAINS, AND MUST BE DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED: when the coordinator's copy and the incoming version genuinely DIFFER, the merge produces a normal `CONFLICT (add/add)` instead of a hard refusal. That is correct — the two sides really do disagree, and main is the source of truth. Do not add a merge driver, a strategy option, or any automatic resolution: state the behaviour in a comment and leave the resolution to the operator. Measured today: 27 of 28 and 20 of 20 real collisions were byte-identical, so this path is the exception, not the rule.

TEST CONTRACT, CORRECTED — this is why the previous implementation passed while its criterion was false. Its tests built temporary repositories that were NOT divergent, so they only ever exercised the fast-forward path. EVERY merge assertion must now build a repository whose coordinator branch carries its own commit, so the merge is NON-fast-forward. Assert: after a full cycle including the closeout, the non-fast-forward merge succeeds with no manual step; it still succeeds on a second cycle; a genuinely differing file produces a normal conflict and NOT a refusal; nothing outside `.shiki` is committed; and no mirror record is deleted.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: `git merge origin/main` in the coordinator still aborts after a loop cycle, now with 'Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge' instead of the untracked variant.
  Measured in a minimal repro (three repositories, identical content, fast-forward vs divergent): staging clears only the fast-forward case; committing clears the divergent case too.
  Root cause: a non-goal in the previous contract — 'the local branch must not advance' — asserted without measurement.
  Reproducible when: a divergent coordinator merges origin/main with no manual step, twice in a row, and a genuinely differing file yields a conflict rather than a refusal.
